questions.question: A video is playing with `playWhenReady = true` when the buffer runs out. What does the player report?
options: `STATE_ENDED`, until more data arrives
`STATE_IDLE`, and `playWhenReady` becomes false
`STATE_READY`, with `isPlaying` still true
`STATE_BUFFERING`, while `playWhenReady` stays true
questions.explanation: Playback state and the user's intent are separate: the state moves to buffering while `playWhenReady` keeps saying the user wants to play. `isPlaying` becomes false during buffering, which is the right signal for a spinner. Idle means not prepared or failed, and ended means the end of the media.

questions.question: ExoPlayer must be accessed from the thread it was created on (its application thread), even though decoding and loading run on an internal playback thread.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: The player is bound to an application Looper, usually the main one, and its listener callbacks are delivered there. Internally, the playback thread drives renderers and loading and talks to the app thread by messages, so the app never calls that thread directly.

questions.question: What does a `Renderer` do inside ExoPlayer?
options: Draws the playback controls on screen
Consumes samples for one track type, such as video, audio or text, and renders them to its output
Downloads media segments from the network
Chooses which bitrate variant to play
questions.explanation: Each renderer handles one kind of track, for example decoding video into a Surface or audio into an AudioTrack. Loading belongs to MediaSources, bitrate choice to the TrackSelector, and controls to the UI module.

questions.question: Playback takes too long to start after the user taps play on a fast network. Which `DefaultLoadControl` setting most directly controls that delay?
options: The back buffer duration
The maximum buffer duration
The amount of media that must be buffered before playback starts
The target buffer size in bytes
questions.explanation: The buffer-for-playback threshold decides how much must be loaded before the player switches to ready and starts. Lowering it starts sooner but raises the chance of an early rebuffer. The maximum and back buffer settings control how much is held later, not startup.

questions.question: You want adaptive streams to never exceed 720p while on a cellular network. What is the idiomatic way?
options: Update `player.trackSelectionParameters` with a maximum video size when the network type changes
Remove the video renderer while on cellular
Build a different MediaItem URL for each resolution
Lower the LoadControl buffer sizes so high bitrates cannot fit
questions.explanation: Track selection parameters constrain what the TrackSelector can pick, and the adaptive selection then chooses among allowed variants by estimated bandwidth. Removing a renderer drops video entirely, and buffer sizes do not cap resolution.

questions.question: Which statements about MediaSources are true? Select all that apply.
options: HLS and DASH need their own Media3 modules to provide the matching MediaSource
A MediaSource draws decoded frames onto the Surface
Each Renderer must be given its own MediaSource
`DefaultMediaSourceFactory` picks the source type from the MediaItem's URI or MIME type
Plain MP4 files are played with a progressive media source
questions.explanation: Adaptive formats live in separate modules, and the default factory chooses HLS, DASH or progressive from the URI or MIME type. A MediaSource provides media structure and samples; renderers do the decoding and drawing, and a single source feeds all of them.

questions.question: If you never call `player.release()`, the player's internal thread and codecs can stay allocated, and hardware decoders are a limited resource.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Release frees the playback thread, decoders and audio output. Devices support only a few simultaneous hardware decoder instances, so leaked players can make later players fail to start.

questions.question: A video feed creates a new ExoPlayer for each visible RecyclerView item. On some devices, later videos fail with decoder initialization errors. What is the best fix?
options: Run each player on a separate background thread
Switch every video to software decoding
Use a small pool of players and attach one to the visible item's surface, releasing or reusing the rest
Raise the LoadControl buffer so decoders start earlier
questions.explanation: Each prepared player can hold a hardware decoder, and devices only have a few, so many players at once exhaust them. Reusing one or two players and swapping MediaItems and surfaces keeps decoder use bounded. Threading or buffering does not change decoder counts, and forcing software decoding costs battery and performance.

questions.question: Users report frequent rebuffering in an HLS stream. Which investigations are useful? Select all that apply.
options: Check whether adaptive selection keeps picking bitrates above what the network sustains
Check whether loading stops early because the LoadControl's buffer limits are being reached
Move player calls to a background thread so the UI is not involved
Increase the number of renderers in the RenderersFactory
Add an `EventLogger` or `AnalyticsListener` to see load events, bandwidth estimates and format switches
questions.explanation: Rebuffering means data is not arriving fast enough or loading paused too early, so look at load timing, bandwidth estimates, buffer limits and chosen variants. More renderers do not add throughput, and the player must still be used from its application thread.

questions.question: A live HLS stream is paused for a long time; on resume it fails with a 'behind live window' error. What is the recommended handling?
options: Recreate the whole Activity
Seek to the default position (the live edge) and call `prepare()` again
Switch to a progressive media source for live content
Increase the back buffer so old segments are kept
questions.explanation: Live playlists only keep a sliding window of segments, so after a long pause the player's position has fallen off the start. The documented fix is to seek to the default position and prepare again. A back buffer stores media already played, and it cannot bring back segments the server has dropped.
